withdrawal: These psutil7.2.2 Windows values are neither residency nor correct64-bit virtual-map size. Do not use them for RAM reclaim/spill/resident-expert conclusions.
mechanism: memory_maps returns VirtualQueryEx.RegionSize (no QueryWorkingSetEx), then Py_BuildValue final unsigned32 I truncates the64-bit SIZE_T.
replacement: windows_memory.observe_memory / mapped_gguf_observation use pointer-width VirtualQueryEx, per-AllocationBase QueryVirtualMemoryInformation.CommitSize and batched no-touch QueryWorkingSetEx. New fields mapped_file_at_ready/mapped_file_after_repeated replace the old names for future executions; old data are not rewritten.
file_backing_vs_private: Host experts4900.50MiB (5.138546688GB) are existing file-backed tensor payload. CPU_Mapped5663.88MiB is a min-to-max file-offset span wrapper over an existing pointer, not a new allocation or resident bytes. Subtracting either from process PrivateUsage to invent an8GB private-heap remainder is invalid.
windows_mapping_behavior: MapViewOfFile maps the full GGUF read-only and unmap_fragment is a Windows no-op. Full virtual map persists even when most tensors offload toGPU. Residency is separately observed, not inferred from this source.

original_simultaneous_app_private_peak.interpretation: Simultaneous numerical relationship from owned raw app samples, not a causal/disjoint partition. Not an8GB unexplained residual.

new_observation: memory-attribution-attempt1.json: OFF/2048 ready and post-three-text snapshots; all4 scans succeeded with0 unavailable allocation/query bytes and no target reads/locks/touches.

new_post_work_findings.interpretation: About13.92GB of the high working set is valid shareable pages from the whole retained GGUF, not just~5.14GB selected host experts. The~13.6GB CPU-VA private commit charge has only~0.774GB valid private allocation pages in this snapshot; it is not13.6GB resident CPU heap. Large nonresident committed private ranges have PAGE_READWRITE|PAGE_WRITECOMBINE protection and scale with GPU allocation, supporting GPU-related commitment without proving allocator callsite or permanent duplicate DRAM.

limits: Scans take~2.7–2.84seconds and are bracketed, not atomic. Some counters change during scan; do not force exact equality of sums/differences. Actual AMD WDDM allocation flags/callsites and physical backing-store duplication are unavailable. The commitment is visible in CPU VA here; it must NOT be claimed absent from CPU allocation totals.
